cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: Electrical systems use power supplies, control devices and output devices to perform useful functions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: Power supplies provide energy: mains (AC 230V, 50Hz) for stationary equipment; batteries (DC) for portable applications.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: Input control devices include switches (toggle, push-button, limit, reed), relays and sensors that control current flow.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: Relays are electrically operated switches: a small control current energises an electromagnet that switches a larger load circuit.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: Output devices convert electrical energy: motors (rotary motion), solenoids (linear motion), lamps and LEDs (light), buzzers (sound).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: AC (alternating current) reverses direction periodically; mains electricity at 50Hz changes direction 100 times per second.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: DC (direct current) flows in one direction only; batteries and solar cells provide DC power.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: Ohm's Law: V = IR; Power = VI = I2R = V2/R; these equations are fundamental to circuit calculations.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: Series circuits: current is the same throughout; voltage is shared across components; total resistance = R1 + R2.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: Parallel circuits: voltage is the same across each branch; current is shared between branches; 1/Rtotal = 1/R1 + 1/R2.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: Fuse ratings and cable sizes must be appropriate for the expected current to prevent overheating and fire.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Electrical Systems
cards.back: Electrical safety: earthing, double insulation, fuses/circuit breakers and residual current devices (RCDs) protect users.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — electrical systems?
cards.back: 1. For Electrical Systems questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Electrical Systems through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
